decisions.title: Choose §6 repair option: flatten dispatch (a) vs retire execute-orchestrator (b) vs Bash-script dispatch surface (c)
decisions.context: T-001 confirms `dispatch_supported: false` and `kill_criterion_triggered: 2` (anchor claims T-0001, T-0002 with `verified` / `very_high` confidence over 3 independent Anthropic doc sources). FR-2 commits the feature to a FULL repair via one of the three §6 options. T-001 (T-0061) explicitly says the Designer's choice is unconstrained by T-001's findings — the choice is a true design decision, not a forced consequence. The codebase-analysis-report's per-option blast-radius enumeration is the load-bearing differentiator (verified per DISSENT-5 resolution: 'evidence not pre-decision').
decisions.reversibility_rationale: Option choice commits the agent inventory (8-file inventory per FR-4), the state-machine ownership location (execute-orchestrator vs recipe-feature-pipeline), and the dispatch surface (agent vs script). Once specialists are re-wired to a new dispatcher, undoing the choice requires migrating live state schemas and re-authoring agent files — costly to reverse.
decisions.blast_radius_rationale: The choice affects every feature-pipeline run going forward (cross-service: execute-orchestrator + 4 specialists + execute-finalize-reconciler + recipe-feature-pipeline + checkpoint/state-transitions schemas). Per CR-0095..CR-0109, options touch 1-5+ files outside the 8-file inventory. Affects all agent-roster consumers of the dispatch surface.
decisions.wardley_stage_rationale: Sub-agent dispatch on Claude Code is custom/bespoke per Anthropic's published guidance (Skills, chain-from-main, agent teams are alternatives). The harness restriction is a fixed property of the substrate (Claude Code), so we are building bespoke within that constraint.

rice.reach_rationale: All 36 agent files in the roster; every feature-pipeline run consumes the dispatch surface. Source: critique DISSENT-3 verified 36 agents.
rice.impact_rationale: Massive — unblocks specialist-isolation pattern (currently lost to single-agent fallback per cluster 5; 7 supporting claims on `conflicts_with` edge from fallback to specialist-isolation). Without resolution, every cc-design pattern that depends on specialist isolation is degraded.
rice.confidence_rationale: Anchor claims are `verified` with `very_high` per critique (3 independent Anthropic sources for T-0001). Mapped to RICE 80% per knowledge-skill rubric (verified + independent provenance). NOT 100% because the choice among (a)/(b)/(c) is itself the live decision — the constraint that forces one of them is settled, but the selection rests on blast-radius evidence + AC-FR-4-a operator disposition.
rice.effort_rationale: Estimate: option (a) ~3 person-weeks (1 file outside inventory + recipe-feature-pipeline state-machine reframing); option (b) ~6+ person-weeks (5+ files outside inventory + AC-FR-4-a gate); option (c) ~3 person-weeks (1 new script + dispatch indirection). Midpoint 4 PW.

options_summary.label: (a) Flatten dispatch hierarchy
options_summary.rationale: Lowest blast-radius outside the 8-file inventory (1 file per CR-0095..CR-0099). Preserves recipe-feature-pipeline as the top-level orchestrator (existing canonical reference per cluster 6) which dispatches the 4 specialists directly; execute-orchestrator becomes an advisor / state-machine documentation. Specialist-isolation pattern (cluster 5) is preserved. The AC-FR-4-a scope-expansion open-item count is minimized (1).

options_summary.label: (b) Retire execute-orchestrator entirely
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — escapes the FR-4 8-file inventory by 5+ files (CR-0100..CR-0108 verified by direct file enumeration in critique DISSENT-5 resolution: KB-documentation-criteria template-assignment table, state-transitions-log-entry-template v1 invariant, pipeline-run-summary-template generated-by, smoke_test_auditing_shared.py test data, auditing-codespaces consumer note). Triggers AC-FR-4-a scope-expansion gate with the largest possible operator surface. Also conflicts with PRD FR-4 (graph edge E-0014 conflicts_with E-0032 with 4 supporting claims).
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected — fails FR-4 8-file inventory by widest margin and triggers AC-FR-4-a scope-expansion gate

options_summary.label: (c) Bash-script dispatch surface
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — execute-orchestrator's runtime tool surface (Read, Write, Bash, Edit per E-0012, three-source-corroborated) CAN run Bash, so the mechanism is physically possible, but a Bash-script dispatcher introduces a new indirection layer (specialists invoked via script, not agent-graph) that breaks the specialist-isolation pattern's audit-trail (cluster 5, AN-0037: 'real audit-trail losses, not just cleanliness'). Comparable blast-radius (1 outside-inventory file) to (a) without the audit-trail advantage. T-001's documented alternatives (Skills, chain-from-main) are stronger options if indirection is desired.
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected — degrades specialist-isolation audit-trail relative to (a) for the same 1-file outside-inventory cost

risks: Single-sourced supporting claim: CR-0108 (option-b blast-radius framing) is single-sourced in the codebase-research, though grounded in direct file enumeration. Critique verdict: verified, but flagged.

DISSENT-2 carry-through: any artifact this decision produces (Blueprint, ADRs, Plan) MUST cite ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 (NOT ADR-0034) for the 4-cycle cap + symmetric D-12 application. Downstream-action required per critique DISSENT-2.
DISSENT-5 carry-through: the recommendation against (b) is grounded in blast-radius evidence, not a pre-decision. The Designer retains discretion subject to AC-FR-4-a operator disposition.
Recipe Step 6 anti-pattern guard: rejection rationales above are named (not straw-men) per knowledge-skill discipline.

Hard-constraint adjacency: NFR-5-a (canonical-reference documentation gap closure) — option (a) requires recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md to absorb state-machine details if execute-orchestrator becomes an advisor.

routing.rationale: ADR-worthiness rule (knowledge skill): reversibility=one_way + blast_radius=tenant + cross-team coordination (recipe-feature-pipeline + agent-roster + checkpoint schema) — all 3 of 3 hold. Architectural. design-composer should author an ADR. Blueprint cc-design subsection enumerates the per-layer agent-graph implications.

decisions.title: How to handle F-7 (mid-session agent registry staleness) for the FR-6 synthetic-test verification step
decisions.context: F-7 is a high-confidence single-instance observation (critique f7_confidence_assessment): the harness loads its agent registry at session start and does NOT hot-reload mid-session. Newly-authored sub-agent files (verified to exist on disk) are not invocable in the same session that authored them; the harness error explicitly enumerates the available agent set. This constrains FR-6's synthetic-test approach but is orthogonal to D-001's §6 selection.
entities_referenced: E-0011 F-7 mid-session agent registry not hot-reloaded
decisions.reversibility_rationale: The verification approach can be revised between runs; no schema or substrate commitment.
decisions.blast_radius_rationale: Scoped to the FR-6 verification step within the feature; does not affect production agent execution.
decisions.wardley_stage_rationale: Synthetic test harness design within a bespoke pipeline; no commodity alternative.

rice.reach_rationale: One verification step; one synthetic minimal feature run.
rice.impact_rationale: High — the verification is the kill-criterion-#2 closure check; if it cannot run, the feature cannot reach Gate-6.
rice.confidence_rationale: F-7 is `partially_verified` per critique (mechanism explicit, population n=1). RICE confidence 50% per knowledge-skill rubric mapping for single-instance + partial verification.
rice.effort_rationale: Half a person-week to write the verification protocol + execute one fresh session.

options_summary.label: (D-002.1) Two-session verification (author in session 1; run in fresh session 2)
options_summary.rationale: Simplest path consistent with the F-7 mechanism (T-0053, T-0054 explicit: 'fresh session' suffices). Plan-author can sequence authoring in an early phase; the verification step in a later phase forces a session boundary. No new harness behavior required. Critic flags this as the downstream_action_required path.

options_summary.label: (D-002.2) Session-restart-in-pipeline step
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — requires the pipeline to orchestrate a session restart, which is not a supported recipe-feature-pipeline primitive today (would require a separate substrate change in the harness or operator-in-the-loop). Higher effort than (D-002.1) with no incremental benefit.
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected — requires harness/operator coordination not provided by current pipeline primitives

options_summary.label: (D-002.3) Author agents in Phase 0; run synthetic test in Phase 1 of a separate fresh run
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected as a default — equivalent to (D-002.1) for the F-7 constraint but requires a fully separate pipeline run, doubling orchestration overhead. Preserve as a fallback if session-boundary scheduling within one run proves infeasible.
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected as default — orchestration overhead higher than (D-002.1) for equivalent F-7 mitigation

risks: DISSENT-4 carry-through: the FR-6 synthetic-test design SHOULD include a sub-question discriminating H-a (baseline-inheritance) vs H-b (memory-field auto-enable) for the Edit-tool mechanism. Per critique DISSENT-4 downstream_action_required, this is non-load-bearing for kill-criterion but is a known open question worth resolving.
F-7 is single-instance (n=1). If the harness has any per-session caching nuance beyond what the error message suggests, the verification protocol may need additional probes. Surface to plan-author.
NFR amendment to PRD may be required to formalize the session-boundary constraint.

routing.rationale: ADR-worthiness rule: reversibility=two_way, blast_radius=component, no cross-team coordination — 0 of 3 hold. NOT ADR-worthy. Operational. Blueprint records the constraint; Plan phases respect the session boundary.

decisions.title: Sweep cleanup posture for execute-finalize-reconciler's `Agent` declaration (cleanup-as-blocker vs inventory-only)
decisions.context: FR-5 sweep (verified by critique: CR-0001-CR-0067 batch B05 + B07) found exactly 2 Agent-declaring agents: execute-orchestrator (primary defect site) and execute-finalize-reconciler (parallel defect, CR-0048-CR-0051 high-confidence inference). T-001 confirms the Agent declaration is a misleading runtime no-op (cleanup-as-blocker check at T-0072). The question is whether to remove the declaration as part of this feature or leave as inventory-only and defer cleanup.
decisions.reversibility_rationale: Removing or restoring an `Agent` declaration in a YAML frontmatter is trivial.
decisions.blast_radius_rationale: One file (execute-finalize-reconciler.md). No schema or cross-agent coupling.
decisions.wardley_stage_rationale: Hygiene cleanup of a misleading declaration; no design novelty.

rice.impact_rationale: Low — removes a misleading-but-runtime-noop declaration. Reduces future confusion; does not change runtime behavior.
rice.confidence_rationale: FR-5 sweep is exhaustive (critique stronger_than_extractor_flagged: 'affected set closed at 2'). 80% per verified-independent rubric.
rice.effort_rationale: Quarter person-week — one frontmatter edit + verification.

options_summary.label: (D-003.1) Remove `Agent` declaration from execute-finalize-reconciler as part of this feature (cleanup-as-blocker)
options_summary.rationale: FR-5 sweep already closed the affected set at 2; both agents are in scope per the feature's repair posture. Removing the declaration in lockstep with execute-orchestrator's repair eliminates the parallel defect surface and prevents future drift. Negligible effort. T-0072 cleanup-as-blocker check supports inclusion.

options_summary.label: (D-003.2) Leave as inventory-only (PRD FR-5 default); cleanup deferred to follow-up
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — leaves a known parallel defect on the floor while shipping the primary repair. AN-0040 explicitly recommends broader cleanup; deferring re-creates the same investigation cost in the follow-up.
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected — leaves a known parallel defect in the codebase post-repair

risks: If execute-finalize-reconciler has any consumer that relies on the (no-op) Agent declaration for documentation/intent signaling, removal could surface a stale assumption. Mitigation: include the rationale in the commit message and the Blueprint.

routing.rationale: ADR-worthiness rule: 0 of 3 hold. Implementation. Plan-author adds as a task in the relevant phase.

decisions.title: Close the recipe-feature-pipeline canonical-reference schema gap (checkpoint.json execution-phase fields)
decisions.context: Cluster 6 (graph) surfaces a pre-existing documentation gap: recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md lines 96-128 reference a checkpoint.json schema that does NOT include the execution-phase fields actually written in flight (execution_pipeline_state_transitions, execution_mode, execution_pipeline_cycle_counters). Codebase-research claims (CR-0061-CR-0080 batch B08, verified) ground this. NFR-5-a requires the canonical reference to update in lockstep with any §6 option change. Independently of D-001, this is a documentary-drift defect with downstream risk for every pipeline run.
entities_referenced: E-0039 NFR-5-a canonical-reference documentation gap closure
E-0069 OI-CR-C checkpoint execution-phase fields undocumented
E-0070 OI-CR-D template invariant + void/-prime undocumented
E-0094 void + -prime de facto log extensions
decisions.blast_radius_rationale: Affects recipe-feature-pipeline (the top-level orchestrator service) and every consumer of the canonical-reference (all 36 agents, plus the state-transitions consumer set).
decisions.wardley_stage_rationale: Canonical schema documentation for a productized pipeline; stable expectations, not bespoke design.

rice.reach_rationale: All 36 agents in the roster consume the canonical-reference contract.
rice.impact_rationale: Medium — closes a real defect but is documentation, not runtime behavior. Prevents future misinterpretation.
rice.confidence_rationale: Codebase-research source verified by direct Grep (critique B08). 80% per verified-independent rubric.
rice.effort_rationale: One person-week to enumerate the in-flight checkpoint.json fields, update SKILL.md, and add template invariants for void/-prime.

options_summary.label: (D-004.1) Close the schema gap in lockstep with the §6 option implementation
options_summary.rationale: NFR-5-a explicitly requires lockstep. Doing this within the same feature satisfies NFR-5-a, prevents post-merge drift, and keeps the recipe-feature-pipeline canonical-reference authoritative. Low effort relative to D-001's effort.

options_summary.label: (D-004.2) Defer to a follow-up documentation feature
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — violates NFR-5-a if the §6 implementation touches the schema. Even if §6 option (a) does not change the schema fields, the documented schema is already stale; deferring is a known-defect-on-the-floor anti-pattern.

risks: OI-CR-D (template invariant + void/-prime undocumented) is the related but distinct sub-finding — the framer recommends closing OI-CR-C and OI-CR-D together to avoid splitting documentation work.
Hard-constraint adjacency: NFR-5-a (must close); NFR-6-a (no-artifact-migration — schema closure is documentation-only, not data migration, so compatible).
If D-001 selects option (b), the schema-gap closure is non-trivially entangled with the state-machine relocation and effort increases.

routing.tertiary: potential ADR if option (b) is selected and schema fields move location
routing.rationale: ADR-worthiness rule: reversibility=two_way, blast_radius=service, no cross-team coordination beyond the recipe-feature-pipeline owner — 1 of 3 hold. Borderline. Default to implementation/operational (Plan + Blueprint); promote to ADR only if D-001=(b) materially changes schema ownership.

decisions.adr_promotion_condition: If D-001 selects option (b), promote D-004 to architectural and author an ADR for the schema-ownership transfer.

decisions.title: Establish a documentation-conventions discipline to prevent ADR mis-attribution recurrence (defer to separate feature)
decisions.context: DISSENT-2 in the critique surfaces a documentary mis-attribution (PRD FR-3-c cites ADR-0034 for symmetric D-12; correct citation is ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 per direct Grep on ADR file contents). The mis-attribution has already been corrected via surgical edit + dissent_evidence in the synthesis. The open question is whether to author an ADR or convention preventing recurrence.
decisions.blast_radius_rationale: Process discipline; affects future PRD/Blueprint authorship habits, not runtime.

rice.impact_rationale: Minimal — DISSENT-2 has already been surgically corrected; the recurrence-prevention question is meta-discipline.
rice.confidence_rationale: Recurrence rate is not measured; single observed instance. 50% per single-instance rubric.
rice.effort_rationale: One person-week to author a documentation-conventions ADR or skill.

options_summary.label: (D-005.1) Defer to a separate documentation-conventions feature (recommended)
options_summary.rationale: Aligned with user-memory project-feedback pattern: belongs in a separate feature, not bundled in dispatch-repair. Avoids scope creep. The corrective action (cite ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 going forward) is already encoded in the critique downstream_action_required and will be carried by D-001's Blueprint.

options_summary.label: (D-005.2) Bundle a documentation-conventions ADR in this feature
options_summary.rejection_rationale: Rejected — scope creep. The dispatch-repair feature is committed to FR-2 + FR-4 + FR-5 + FR-6 + NFR-5-a; adding a conventions ADR widens scope without strengthening the kill-criterion-#2 closure.
options_summary.rejection_named: rejected — out of scope for kill-criterion-#2 closure

risks: If deferred indefinitely, the same mis-attribution pattern could recur. Mitigation: surface as an open item that downstream Synthesizer + Blueprint must respect by citing ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 consistently.

routing.secondary: Synthesizer note: downstream artifacts MUST cite ADR-0017 + ADR-0033 (carry through DISSENT-2 resolution)
routing.rationale: ADR-worthiness rule: 0 of 3 hold. Not ADR-worthy in this feature. Defer.
